137
RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday,  the May 16, 2006/Vaisakha 26, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Civil Aviation; Company Affairs; Finance; Heavy Industries
and Public Enterprises; Petroleum and Natural Gas; Tourism
and Culture; Water Resources)
Total number of questions — 20
Per capita burden of loans
†*441. SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL: Will the Minister of
FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) what is the per capita burden of loans
in the country as on date;
(b) the amount paid against interest on
loans during the last three years and current
financial year so far; and
(c) the steps taken or proposed to be
taken by Government to reduce the same?
Rationalisation of tariff regime
*442. SHRI HARISH RAWAT:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that for several
product lines, the existing tariff regime
results in higher import duty rate on raw
materials/intermediates than on finished
products, thereby discouraging value addition
by domestic manufacturers;
(b) whether the Ministry have a list of
all product lines, which face inverted duty
structure;
(c) what action is proposed to
rationalize the tariff regime to address this
anomaly; and
(d) whether Government propose to do
away with Early Harvest List in Regional
Trading Agreements (RTAs) as the Early
Harvest List of goods in RTAs create
inverted duty structure?
Allotment of petrol pumps to
dependants of Kargil war
martyrs
†*443. SHRI LAXMINARAYAN
SHARMA:  Will the Minister of
PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have formulated a plan to allot dealership of
petrol pumps and LPG to the widows of the
brave martyrs of Kargil war;
(b) if so, how many widows/dependants
of martyr soldiers have been allotted
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

138
dealership of petrol pumps and LPG till
date and how many of them are still left;
and
(c) the number of such persons in
Madhya Pradesh allotted petrol pumps and
LPG dealership?
Domestic LPG consumers in
Rajasthan
*444. DR. GYAN PRAKASH
PILANIA: Will the Minister of
PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be
pleased to state:
(a) number of domestic LPG consumers
in Rajasthan and Jaipur;
(b) quantum in metric tonnes of cooking
gas required every month in Rajasthan;
(c) whether there is shortage of domestic
LPG in Rajasthan;
(d) whether new domestic LPG
connections have been stopped;
(e) whether Government are aware that
LPG meant for domestic consumption is
being diverted to hotels, restaurants,
automobile filling stations;
(f) if so, steps taken to stop this
pilferage;
(g) whether there is acute shortage of
LPG cylenders in the country;
(h) number of persons on the waiting
list for LPG connections, in Rajasthan, till
date; and
(i) by when, this backlog is likely to be
cleared?
Cancellation of Operation Safety
Certificate of AI
*445. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the governing
body for global airlines, International Air
Transport Association (IATA) has cancelled
Air India's Operation Safety Certificate for
failing to meet International Operations
Safety Audit (IOSA) standards; and
(b) whether Government have made any
investigations to find out why the Indian flag
carrier has failed to meet IOSA and if so,
the action proposed?
Filling of backlog vacancies in
Departments under M/o Civil Aviation
*446. SHRI PRAVEEN
RASHTRAPAL:  Will the Minister of
CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) the backlog of vacancies as on 31st
March, 2004 in various Departments under
his Ministry;
(b) whether, special drive was carried
out to fill in the above backlog vacancies;
(c) if so, the number of vacancies filled
in during the last two years, Department-
wise; and
(d) what are the backlog vacancies as
on 31st March, 2006?
New guidelines for grievances of bank
customers
*447. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the
Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether RBI has framed new
guidelines/rules to address the grievances
of bank customers;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) what is the action plan of Government
to control addition of unjustified charges and
making of harassing calls by the bank
officials, etc.?

139
Financial package for Himachal
Pradesh
*448. SHRI SURESH BHARDWAJ:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) the status/position of the financial
package/assistance announced by the Prime
Minister for Himachal Pradesh on the 28th
May, 2005 while on a visit to the State; and
(b) the number of schemes sanctioned
and funds provided for the same during the
year 2005- 06 by the Central Government?
Package for Rural Co-operatives
*449. SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether a proposal of Rs.13600
crore package for Rural Co-operatives was
approved during December, 2005;
(b) if so, the purpose of the above fund

717
RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for WRITTEN ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday, the May 16, 2006/Vaisakha 26, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Civil Aviation; Company Affairs; Finance; Heavy Industries
and Public Enterprises; Petroleum and Natural Gas; Tourism and
Culture; Water Resources)
Total number of questions — 155
Unused runways at airports
3176. DR. M.A.M. RAMASWAMY:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether a large number of runways
at different airports in the country are not
in use;
(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise
and the reasons therefor;
(c) whether any action is being taken to
make them usable;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Rehabilitation of slum around
Mumbai airport
3177. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether his Ministry has prepared
a blueprint to rehabilitate the eligible slum
dwellers on the periphery of Mumbai
airport;
(b) if so, the details thereof including
the total number of slum dwellers to be
rehabilitated and the total cost involved;
and
(c) whether Government have fixed
time-schedule for the rehabilitation work,
if so, by when it will be completed?
Study on new airport at Mumbai
3178. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to refer to answer to Unstarred
Question 1365 given in the Rajya Sabha on
6th December, 2005 and state:
(a) whether the simulation study of
conflict free operations for existing airport
at Mumbai and proposed airport at Navi
Mumbai undertaken by International Civil
Aviation Organization (ICAO), City and
Industrial Development Corporation of
Maharashtra Ltd. (CIDCO) and Airports
Authority of India (AAI) has since been
completed; and
(b) if so, the details thereof and if not,
by when the study is likely to be completed?

718
Recommendation of KAW Committee
3179. SHRIMATI SYEDA ANWARA
TAIMUR: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether the KAW Committee
favoured the Directorate-General of Civil
Aviation as the sole apex body for safety
and economic revolution of the aviation
sector;
(b) if so, Government's reaction thereto;
(c) whether it is a fact that some of the
suggestions of the KAW Committee are in
conflict with the plan of the Ministry; and
(d) if so, what are the areas of difference
and the manner in which Government
propose to sort out the matter?
Delay in evening flights
3180. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA
RAO: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) the reasons for the routine delays of
all Indian Airlines flights which take off
after 4 p.m. every day;
(b) whether it is a fact that the Indian
Airlines management is unable to cope with
the delays which build up after every flight;
(c) whether it is also a fact that every
Indian Airlines flight from Delhi to
Hyderabad in the evening has been late by
a minimum of two hours every day in the
last three months;
(d) whether any effort will be made to
monitor the delays which have now become
routine and expected and definite every day;
and
(e) the steps proposed to consider ways
to reduce such definite delays?
Increasing air services
†3181. SHRI DILIP SINGH JUDEV:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of air routes in the
country wherein domestic air services have
been increased;
(b) the names of States benefited by
such increase;
(c) the details of existing air routes
alongwith new routes where respective
proposals for increasing flight services and
introducing air service are under
consideration during the year 2006-07; and
(d) the details of proposals received
from State Governments in this regard
alongwith those approved and pending as
on 31st January, 2006, State-wise?
Unutilised bilateral agreements
3182. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that about 47 of
the 101 airlines bilateral agreements signed
between India and other countries are
unutilised;
(b) whether it is also a fact that of the
54 operational bilaterals, carriers from both
countries are offering services only in 26
cases;
(c) if so, whether it is a fact that the
severe dearth of flights coupled with
unviable locations are the reasons for a
number of bilateral pacts lying unused; and
(d) the steps Government propose to
take to make use of all bilateral pacts?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
